Serenade Of The Seas Review

Review of Serenade Of The Seas

The 2003-built Serenade of the Seas cruise ship is the third Radiance-class Royal Caribbean liner, with sister ships Jewel OTS, Radiance OTS, and Brilliance OTS.

The vessel (IMO number 9228344) is currently Bahamas-flagged (MMSI 311492000) and registered in Nassau.

History - construction and ownership

Royal Caribbean International (RCI) is a US passenger shipping company, a trademarked travel brand, and a subsidiary of Royal Caribbean Group (RCG/shipowner). RCI was established in 1968 and currently holds over one-fifth of the global cruise market. The brand also operates RCG's largest fleet by both vessel count and GT tonnage (ship size and capacity).

All RCI ships have names ending with "of the Seas".

The 2500-passenger Serenade OTS fits within the Panama Canal's Panamax dimensions. This also means that all Radiance-class ships can access most regions worldwide. These mid-sized vessels offer numerous options, from dining to entertainment, and feature approximately 3 acres (1.2 hectares) of exterior glass, including glass-walled elevators with ocean views.

Decks and Cabins

Serenade Of The Seas staterooms (1074 total, in 32 grades) include 61 Suites, 517 Balcony, 247 Oceanview, and 249 Inside (3 Single). Most cabins are sized 165-190 ft2 (15-18 m2). Most cabin balconies are sized 45 ft2 (4 m2). The smallest is the Studio Interior (110 ft2 / 10 m2). The largest is the Royal Suite (1000 ft2 / 93 m2 plus a 105 ft2 / 10 m2 terrace). Wheelchair-accessible cabins total 19.

The ship has 13 decks, of which 12 are passenger-accessible and 8 contain cabins.

Shipboard dining options - Food and Drinks

Reflections is the ship's two-deck-high formal dining room. The focal point of its decor is a cascading waterfall. For dinner, guests can choose between assigned early or late seating, or opt for My Time Dining, allowing flexible dining between 6 and 9:30 pm. Passengers selecting My Time Dining must pre-pay gratuities. The Reflections restaurant operates under an open-seating policy for breakfast and lunch. The cuisine is varied and includes alternative menu options for guests with restricted diets.

Windjammer Cafe is the main buffet venue. It is open for breakfast, lunch, afternoon snacks, and informal dinner. Numerous stations serve pasta, burgers, salads, and desserts. Portofino and Chops Grille are the ship's alternative restaurants.

Chops is a steakhouse venue with an open kitchen. While Chops is enjoyable, the highlight of onboard dining is often considered Portofino, with signature dishes such as tiger shrimp risotto and spaghetti with lobster sauce. Both Chops Grille and Portofino charge a per-person service fee (US$30 at Chops and US$20 at Portofino).

Below is the complete list of Serenade of the Seas restaurants and food bars.

  • Reflections Restaurant (1096-seat aft Dining Room with two smaller private dining rooms: 30-seat Mirage and 102-seat Illusions)
  • Windjammer Cafe Lido buffet restaurant (638 seats; offers Early Breakfast at 6:30 am, Breakfast between 7-11:30 am, Lunch 11:30 am-3:30 pm, and Dinner 6:30-9 pm)
  • Chops Grille (95-seat specialty restaurant; reservations recommended)
  • Giovanni's Table (Italian specialty restaurant; reservations recommended)
  • Chefs Table (12-seat gourmet dining room)
  • Park Cafe (complimentary deli restaurant serving the Solarium area)
  • Izumi (Asian specialty restaurant)
  • Rita's Cantina (84-seat Mexican specialty restaurant)

Shipboard entertainment options - Fun and Sport

There is no shortage of entertainment onboard Serenade of the Seas. Cultural and educational activities such as digital photography classes and wine-tasting seminars are offered, along with horse races, blackjack tournaments, elaborate production shows in the Tropical Theater, and informal dancing in the atrium lobby.

Those looking for more nightlife can visit the Vortex Disco on Deck 13 (featuring a revolving bar), a popular venue for singles. The DJ plays a wide variety of music, from Top 40 hits to classic dance tracks, late into the evening.

Additional amenities include complimentary 24-hour room service, supervised youth programs, Internet/Wi-Fi access, and laundry services.

Below is the complete list of Serenade of the Seas lounges, clubs, and other entertainment venues for kids, teens, and adults.

  • Tropical Theatre (915-seat venue featuring grand production shows with dance, acrobatics, comedy, and games)
  • Vortex Disco and Nightclub (126-seat venue with revolving bar)
  • Photo Gallery and Shop; Art Gallery
  • The Centrum (social hub featuring aerial acrobatics entertainment); Card Room; Next Cruise Lounge; Safari Lounge (320-seat venue hosting religious services and auctions); Crown Lounge (formerly Diamond Club Lounge & Bar for past guests only); Concierge Club (for suite guests and select loyalty members); Viking Crown Lounge and Nightclub
  • R Bar (59-seat cocktail bar); Cafe Latte-tudes Bar (46-seat specialty coffee bar serving Starbucks Coffee); Crown and Castle English Pub (sports bar); Vintages Bar (wine bar); Schooner Bar (74-seat piano bar); Sky Bar
  • Centrum Boutiques (duty-free shops offering clothes, perfumes, accessories, jewelry, logo souvenirs, and General Store items including alcohol and cigarettes)
  • Casino Royale (258-seat casino)
  • Royal Caribbean Online Center (Internet computer room; 24-hour access)
  • Vitality at Sea Spa and Fitness Center; 3 Jacuzzis; 2 swimming pools
  • Solarium lounge (includes Cafe Bar, pool bar, and adults-only pool area)
  • Outdoor movie screen; Cinema (53-seat venue)
  • Video Games Arcade; Fuel Teen Disco club; Royal Babies and Tots Nursery
  • Adventure Beach; Adventure Ocean kids lounge area
  • Sports Court (golf simulator, table tennis, basketball court); Jogging Track; Rock-climbing Wall; Fairways of Serenade Mini-Golf Course

Itineraries

Serenade of the Seas itinerary program includes 7-day voyages in the Caribbean (roundtrips from Cartagena Colombia and Colon Panama during winter 2025-2026) and Alaska itineraries (during summer) departing roundtrip from Vancouver (BC Canada).

Following the Coronavirus crisis, Serenade OTS restarted operations on July 19, 2021, with an Alaska roundtrip from Seattle WA. The 7-day Alaska Glacier itinerary included ports such as Sitka, Icy Strait Point, Juneau, and Ketchikan, as well as scenic cruising in Tracy Arm Fjord (Endicott Arm and Dawes Glacier). Serenade became the industry's first ship to resume operations in Alaska and RCI's second ship to restart services in the USA (after Freedom OTS from PortMiami on July 2).

After the Alaska season, Serenade OTS was scheduled for an Australia-New Zealand deployment (winter 2021-2022 / October-March, homeported in Sydney NSW), followed by Alaska in 2022 (from Vancouver) and Bahamas-Western Caribbean voyages from Tampa Florida (2022-2023). However, the Australian program was canceled and replaced with Caribbean sailings (4-5-day roundtrips from Tampa) to Mexico (Cozumel, Costa Maya) and the Bahamas (Nassau, CocoCay).

In October 2021, RCI announced the company's first World Cruise (December 2023 - September 2024), which also became RCI's longest itinerary and one of the world's longest around-the-world voyages (274 nights). Read more in the ship's Wiki section.

In winter 2026-2027, the ship is scheduled to operate 7-day Mexican Riviera roundtrips from San Diego (California USA). The itinerary visits La Paz, Cabo San Lucas, and Ensenada. Prices (when bookings opened in February 2025) started at US$800 per person (double occupancy).

Serenade Of The Seas Wiki

Serenade OTS is one of Royal Caribbean's Radiance-class liners, with sister ships Brilliance, Jewel, and Radiance.

Serenade was built at Meyer Werft's Papenburg Shipyard. The vessel's godmother was the always charming and smiling Whoopi Goldberg (US actress and Oscar winner). The naming ceremony was held in NYC on August 22, 2003. The inaugural voyage started on August 25. The maiden season (2003) was based on 5-6-night roundtrips from New York to Canada and New England (USA), after which (in November) the ship was deployed in the Caribbean and homeported in San Juan, Puerto Rico.

All Radiance-class ships were constructed in compliance with Panamax standards, allowing them to transit through the Panama Canal. Serenade, along with all her sisterships, is powered by gas turbines instead of diesel engines. This design makes the vessels more fuel-efficient while also reducing emissions of harmful gases.

Serenade OTS refurbishments review

Drydock 2025

The ship's last drydock refurbishment was in March 2025 and was conducted at the Grand Bahama Shipyard in Freeport.

The project included regularly scheduled routine maintenance, technical and safety/classification inspections, hull cleaning and repainting, and minor updates to public areas.

Drydock 2022

The 2022 drydock included mainly routine maintenance works (hull cleaning and painting, mechanical and machinery inspections and upgrades), renovations to outdoor spaces (sundeck and swimming pools), and recarpeting of all indoor public areas (hallways, bars, lounges).

Drydock 2012

The list of deck plan changes after the 2012 drydock refurbishment included:

  • Upgraded cabin amenities (flat-screen TVs, bathrooms with improved shower floors)
  • Jumbotron (large poolside LED screen for movies, located near the main pool on the Lido Deck)
  • New lounges ("Diamond" and "Concierge")
  • New specialty dining venues with an additional charge (Giovanni's Table/Italian Trattoria, Izumi/Asian cuisine, Rita's Cantina/Mexican cuisine, Chef's Table/5-course VIP dining)
  • Nursery
  • Upgraded Centrum Atrium entertainment options (acrobatic shows, LED screens)
  • R Bar (retro 1960s-themed, replacing the old Lobby Bar), Vintages Bar (wine bar), and an English pub
  • Wi-Fi coverage upgraded to shipwide
  • Digital signage boards installed

Comic-Con Cruise 2025

Serenade OTS is RCI's first ship to host a Comic-Con - the annual event organized by San Diego Comic-Con International (founded in 1970 as the "Golden State Comic Book Convention").

The special voyage (February 5-9, 2025, roundtrip from Tampa Florida) is a full-ship charter by Entertainment Cruise Productions (a Clayton, Missouri-based company specializing in themed voyages).

The industry's first Comic-Con cruise ship experience will feature various small-group events (including Q&A sessions, trivia, and fun contests), video gaming competitions, and themed parties (dancing, karaoke, cosplay/costume play, DJs).

When the announcement was made (in July 2023), prices (per person) ranged from US$990 (interior cabin) to US$5620 (Royal Suite) based on double occupancy, while single occupancy started at US$1240 (interior).

World Cruise 2023-2024 (RCI's first around-the-world voyage)

In October 2021, RCI announced the company's first World Cruise, which is also Royal Caribbean's longest itinerary and one of the world's longest around-the-world voyages.

The 274-night itinerary (themed "Ultimate World Cruise", from December 10, 2023, through September 10, 2024) scheduled for Serenade OTS is roundtrip from Miami and visits 150 ports and islands (57 new for RCI) in 65 countries across 7 continents.

Prices started at US$60,000 per person (double occupancy), inclusive of Business Class flights, a pre-cruise 5-star hotel stay (overnight), premium transportation (airport-hotel-ship transfers), and onboard gratuities. Loyalty program members at the Platinum level and above received bonus perks including a Shore Excursion Package (7 guided land tours), Deluxe Beverage Package, complimentary Wi-Fi Internet (VOOM Surf & Stream), and free laundry services (Wash & Fold).

Shorter itineraries/world cruise segments included:

  • 64-day (Dec 10 - Feb 11) "Round the Horn: Americas and Antarctica Expedition" itinerary visits 36 ports/islands, 3 continents, and destinations in the Caribbean, Central and South America, Cape Horn, Antarctica, Rio de Janeiro (New Year's Eve overnight), Los Angeles (overnight).
  • 87-day (Feb 11 - May 9) "Wonders of Asia and the Pacific Expedition" itinerary visits 40 ports/islands, 3 continents, and destinations in North America (Hawaii), Oceania (French Polynesia), New Zealand, Australia, Asia (Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, India, Japan).
  • 63-day (May 9 - July 10) "Middle East Treasures and Marvels of the Med Expedition" itinerary visits 44 ports, 3 continents, and destinations in Arabia (Dubai, Jordan), Africa (Egypt), Mediterranean (Turkey, Greece, Italy, France, Spain), Adriatic (Croatia).
  • 63-day (July 10 - Sept 10) "Capitals of Culture" itinerary visits 40 ports, 3 continents and destinations in the Mediterranean (Spain, Morocco), Baltic (Russia/St Petersburg, Norway), with the Transatlantic crossing from Europe to the USA (via Iceland and NYC New York) ending in PortMiami.

The Balcony stateroom cost USD 75,000 ($136 pp per day), the 4-passenger Royal Suite cost USD 760,000. ~70% of the ship was booked within the first week. Full-paid early bookings (made by January 6, 2023) receive a 10% discount. Additional costs include taxes-fees-port charges (USD 4667 USD pp).

The above-listed itinerary segments were open for booking on Feb 10, 2022. In April 2023 were open for booking more segments:

  • 26-day (Dec 10, 2023 - Jan 5, 2024) "Ultimate Caribbean and South America" itinerary (Miami to Buenos Aires) visits CocoCay Bahamas, Cozumel Mexico, Oranjestad Aruba, Willemstad Curacao, Kralendijk Bonaire, Bridgetown Barbados, St George Grenada, Cayenne (Devil Island French Guiana), Brazil (Fortaleza, Recife, Rio de Janeiro, Copacabana) and Montevideo Uruguay.
  • 18-day (Jan 5-23) "Ultimate South America and Antarctica" itinerary (Buenos Aires to Valparaiso-Santiago) visits Puerto Madryn Argentina, Port Stanley Falklands, Antarctica (Gerlache Strait, Paradise Bay, Schollaert Channel, Elephant Island), Cape Horn Chile, Ushuaia Argentina, Punta Arenas Chile, Magellan Straits, Chilean Fjords.
  • 19-day (Jan 23 - Feb 11) "Ultimate Central and South America" itinerary (Valparaiso-Santiago to Los Angeles) visits ports in Chile (Coquimbo-La Serena, Arica), Peru (Pisco-Machu Picchu, Callao-Lima), Ecuador (Manta), Costa Rica (Puntarenas), Nicaragua (San Juan del Sur) and Mexico (Cabo San Lucas, Ensenada).
  • 29-day (Feb 11 - Mar 11) "Ultimate Hawaii, Tahiti and Australia" itinerary (Los Angeles to Brisbane) visits ports in Hawaii USA (Maui-Lahaina), Hawaii-Kailua Kona, Oahu-Honolulu), French Polynesia (Moorea, Papeete Tahiti), New Zealand (Auckland, Russel-Bay of Islands) and NSW Australia (Sydney, Newcastle).
  • 16-day (Mar 11-27) "Ultimate Australia and Southeast Asia" itinerary (Brisbane to Hong Kong China) visits ports in Queensland Australia (Airlie Beach, Cairns), Indonesia (Lombok, Benoa) and The Philippines (Manila, Subic Bay-Luzon).
  • 12-day (Mar 27 - Apr 8) "Ultimate China, Japan and South Korea" itinerary (Hong Kong to Tianjin-Beijing China) visits ports in Taiwan China (Keelung-Taipei), Japan (Ishigaki, Naha) and South Korea (Busan, Jeju Island, Incheon-Seoul).
  • 16-day (Apr 8-24) "Ultimate Japan, Vietnam and Singapore" itinerary (Beijing to Singapore) visits ports in Japan (Nagasaki, Kagoshima, Yokohama-Tokyo, Shimizu, Osaka-Kyoto) and Vietnam (Nha Trang, Phu My-Saigon).
  • 15-day (Apr 24 - May 9) "Ultimate India, Sri Lanka and Malaysia" itinerary (Singapore to Dubai) visits ports in Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur (Port Klang-Kuala Lumpur, Penang), Sri Lanka (Hambantota, Colombo), India (Cochin, Mormugao-Goa, Mumbai) and UAE (Abu Dhabi).
  • 18-day (May 9-27) "Ultimate Jordan, Egypt and Israel" itinerary (Dubai to Piraeus-Athens Greece) visits Salalah Oman, Aqaba-Petra Jordan, Safaga Egypt, Suez Canal (transit), Alexandria Egypt, Ashdod-Jerusalem Israel, Limassol Cyprus Greece.
  • 11-day (May 27 - Jun 7) "Ultimate Bulgaria, Romania and Turkey" Black Sea itinerary (Piraeus-Athens to Istanbul) visits Kusadasi-Ephesus Turkey, Burgas Bulgaria, Constanta Romania, Varna Bulgaria, Trabzon Turkey
  • 13-day (Jun 7-20) "Ultimate Greece, Turkey and Italy" itinerary (Istanbul to Ravenna-Venice) visits ports in Greece (Thessaloniki, Chios Island), Turkey (Bodrum), Greece (Rhodes Island, Mykonos Island, Santorini Island, Chania-Souda, Crete Island, Katakolon-Olympia, Corfu Island) and Italy (Bari).
  • 11-day (Jun 20 - Jul 1) "Ultimate Italy, Croatia and Malta" Adriatic Sea itinerary (Ravenna-Venice and Civitavecchia-Rome) visits Trieste Italy, Koper Slovenia, Croatia (Zadar, Split, Dubrovnik), Kotor Montenegro, Valletta Malta, Italy (Catania Sicily, Naples).
  • 9-day (Jul 1-10) "Ultimate Italy, France and Spain" itinerary (Civitavecchia-Rome to Barcelona) visits ports in Italy (Carrara-Florence/Pisa, Portofino), France (Ajaccio Corsica, Cannes, Villefranche-Nice, Toulon) and Balearic Spain (Palma de Mallorca).
  • 16-day (Jul 10-26) "Ultimate Spain, Morocco and France" itinerary (Barcelona to Southampton England UK) visits ports in Spain (Valencia, Cartagena, Malaga), Morocco (Casablanca-Marrakesh, Agadir), Portugal (Lisbon, Leixoes-Oporto), Spain (Vigo), Ireland (Cobh-Cork), France (Cherbourg, Le Havre-Paris).
  • 15-day (Jul 26 - Aug 10) "Ultimate Denmark, Germany and Sweden" Baltic Sea itinerary (Southampton to Copenhagen Denmark) visits Xeebruge-Bruges/Brussels Belgium, Skagen Denmark, Warnemunde-Berlin Germany, Riga Latvia, Tallinn Estonia, Helsinki Finland, Sweden (Stockholm, Visby), Klaipeda Lithuania, Ronne Denmark, Kiel Germany.
  • 9-day (Aug 10-19) "Ultimate Norwegian Fjords" itinerary (Copenhagen to Amsterdam Holland) visits Aarhus Denmark and ports in Norway (Oslo, Kristiansand, Haugesund, Olden, Alesund, Bergen).
  • 22-day (Aug 19 - Sep 10) "Ultimate Iceland, Greenland and Caribbean" Transatlantic itinerary (Amsterdam to Miami) visits Reykjavik Iceland, Greenland (Qaqortoq, Nuuk), St Johns Newfoundland Canada, NYC New York, King's Wharf Bermuda, CocoCay Bahamas.

Ultimate World Cruise itinerary change (2024)

In February 2024, RCI allowed the Ultimate World Cruise passengers (including those booked on the affected segments) to vote on the itinerary changes necessitated by the Red Sea crisis.

The company offered two route change options - "Immersive Africa" and "Africa & Greece", with the same length (43 nights, between May 9th and June 20th, 2024).
